text:
Alex: quick heads up — noticed a perf regression after yesterday's autotuner change. selector picked flashv3 for head_dim=30 on sm90 but for small seq lens (<=64) the token latency is much worse vs flashv2. KV-cache warmup seems to amplify it.

Maria: can you paste the numbers + env?

Alex: repro env:
```
GPU: sm90
model: rext-large (head_dim=30)
batch=1, microbatch=1
seqlen: 8 / 16 / 64
```
p50 token latency (cold start -> steady state):
```
v3 (chosen): seqlen=64 -> 18.2ms
v2 (fallback): seqlen=64 -> 9.1ms
v3: seqlen=16 -> 22.5ms
v2: seqlen=16 -> 10.8ms
```
nvprof/trace shows heavy prefetch stalls and low SM occupancy for v3 at these shapes — looks like head_dim(30) misaligns kernel tiling so we get inefficient CTAs + extra mem ops.

Sam: yeah that sounds like head-mod / warp alignment problem. autotuner cost model assumes steady-state throughput and doesn't account for warmup or misaligned CTA overhead. for non-causal vs causal? this is showing up on causal path (kv-prefetch + single-token steps).

Alex: repro script:
```
python perf/run_infer.py --model rext-large --head 30 --seqlen 64 --device cuda:0 --mode causal
```

Priya: suggestion: add a simple head_mod heuristic to selector: if head_dim % 32 != 0 and seqlen <= 64 prefer flashv2; also weight the cost with a "warmup_penalty" for short completions. cheap fix until we add warmup-aware cost model.

Alex: pushed hotfix branch hotfix/sdpa-headmod with head_mod gate + seqlen cutoff. testing canary now.

deploybot: deploy: canary rollout started for hotfix/sdpa-headmod -> gpu-pool-3 (2 nodes)

Maria: run against other heads? any regressions?

Sam: quick smoke across head=16/32/48: no perf regressions. adding unit tests for selector to cover head_mod cases.

Alex: plan: merge hotfix after 12h canary if metrics are green, then implement warmup-aware cost in next sprint. opening PR with perf traces: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/1234

Priya: happy to run broader workload sweep on our infra. ping me.

Alex: :rocket:
